notes: This catalog slice focuses on 48 GB workstation GPUs that can bridge the gap between 24-32 GB cards and 64-128+ GB unified-memory or datacenter systems.
Manufacturer specifications are used for architecture, memory, bandwidth, power and interfaces. Marketplace and reseller prices are point-in-time observations and are not treated as MSRP.
LLM model-fit guidance is approximate because runtime overhead, KV cache, context length, quantization format and offload strategy materially affect usable capacity.

hardware.release_context: 48GB W7800 configuration appeared in channel listings in 2026
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximately 30B-class 4-bit models fit comfortably; some larger weight-only quantizations may fit, but 70B-class operation is runtime/context dependent and should not be assumed from VRAM capacity alone.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: Runtime dependent; practical paths include ROCm/HIP and Vulkan-based engines. Verify the exact ROCm support matrix and model backend before purchase.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: High memory bandwidth plus 48GB capacity make this more LLM-relevant than the original 32GB W7800. The primary risk is software/backend maturity versus CUDA.
hardware.performance_per_watt_note: 864 GB/s at 260W is strong for a 48GB active-cooled workstation card; decode performance still requires model-specific benchmarking.
hardware.cost_efficiency_note: Current Canadian channel pricing is substantially below observed 48GB NVIDIA Ampere listings, but software compatibility can outweigh hardware price for CUDA-dependent workloads.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: medium-low; 260W board power is manageable in a workstation but materially heavier than 70-130W edge/SFF options.

pricing.note: Backordered reseller listing; another Canadian channel listing was CA$3,410.18 with availability by email.

hardware.physical_constraints: 11 in / 280 mm full-height card; AMD currently lists both double-slot and triple-slot W7900 variants, so exact board variant must be checked.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 48GB capacity is well suited to 30B-class quantized models and large-context smaller models; 70B-class 4-bit fit depends on runtime overhead and context/KV cache.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: ROCm/HIP and Vulkan engines support common quantized inference paths, but exact model/runtime support should be validated before purchase.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Excellent raw memory subsystem for a workstation GPU; acquisition cost and ROCm/backend maturity are the main tradeoffs.
hardware.performance_per_watt_note: Same 864 GB/s memory bandwidth as W7800 48GB at a higher 295W board power, with substantially more compute.
hardware.cost_efficiency_note: The current Canada-located used asking price observed in this pass is poor relative to the W7800 48GB and should be treated as a market warning, not a recommendation.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; nearly 300W board power plus workstation host overhead.

pricing.note: Canada-located used-like-new listing; no returns accepted. This is an asking price, not a completed-sale valuation.

hardware.nvlink: 2-way; NVIDIA documents up to 96GB combined memory for supported applications
hardware.model_size_practicality: 48GB is a strong single-GPU capacity tier for 30B-class quantized models and large contexts; some larger quantized models can fit depending on runtime overhead.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: Broad CUDA ecosystem support for FP16/BF16 and common INT8/INT4/GGUF quantized inference paths; application support varies by engine.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Still technically attractive because 48GB ECC VRAM, 768GB/s bandwidth and mature CUDA support remove many integration risks found on cheaper alternatives.
hardware.performance_per_watt_note: 300W is high for off-grid use, but the mature CUDA stack can deliver better effective utilization than less-supported hardware.
hardware.cost_efficiency_note: Current used Canadian-visible asking prices remain high; compare against newer 32GB cards and 128GB unified-memory systems before buying.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; 300W GPU power plus host load.

pricing.note: Representative pre-owned RTX A6000 listing visible around CA$5,350; seller, shipping and condition vary.

hardware.nvlink: 2-way; NVIDIA documents up to 96GB combined GDDR6 and up to 100GB/s transfer for supported applications
hardware.cooling: variant dependent; workstation cards are active while server variants can be passive and require directed airflow
hardware.model_size_practicality: 48GB remains useful for 30B-class quantized models and capacity-heavy workloads even though Turing compute is now several generations old.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: Mature CUDA-era support for common quantized inference paths, but newer kernels/features may increasingly target Ampere and later architectures.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: A capacity-first used option. It is slower and less efficient than newer 48GB GPUs, but can make sense if acquisition price drops far enough.
hardware.performance_per_watt_note: 672GB/s at roughly 260W graphics power is respectable for its generation but trails newer cards in compute efficiency.
hardware.cost_efficiency_note: The current representative used listing is materially cheaper than RTX A6000 asking prices, making RTX 8000 worth tracking when 48GB capacity matters more than newest-generation kernels.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low; high board power and potentially passive server cooling on some secondary-market variants.

pricing.note: Representative pre-owned 48GB RTX 8000 server card listing. Cross-border taxes, warranty, cooling variant and condition must be checked.
